residualFailedRequests.note: Raw harness output (docs/migration/.scratch/p5.2-attempt2c/visual-suite.json) is 'status: fail (4 flagged)' because its own top-level status is anyFail-on-any-residual; this evidence file's checks above and G5.4 pass because every residual is proven to be a Next.js RSC prefetch cancelled by navigation/teardown timing, present identically on A, and 200 on direct re-request -- the literal SPEC-04 §7 condition for a residual counting as explained.

entries.explanation: Next.js client-side <Link> hover/viewport prefetch of /demo, issued by every page that links to the demo CTA, raced against page-teardown at the end of the harness's own navigation/wait step and aborted before the response was consumed by the page. Proven with a standalone Playwright probe (/tmp/rsc-probe.mjs, same Chromium binary /opt/pw-browsers/chromium, same proxy CA pin as run.mjs, run outside the reviewed harness) navigating revenue-platform and blog-index at both viewports on both origins: (1) RSC prefetch markers -- the captured request carries `_rsc=<token>` in its URL and the request headers `rsc: 1`, `next-router-prefetch: 1`, `next-url: <the page's own path>`, `next-router-state-tree: ...` -- textbook Next.js App Router prefetch headers, not a normal navigation; (2) cancellation, not a real error -- Playwright's own requestfailed handler reports failure text exactly `net::ERR_ABORTED` (never a 4xx/5xx or a DNS/TLS failure) on both A and B, and which specific prefetch aborts vs. completes varies nondeterministically between runs (in the probe, /demo aborted on A for revenue-platform/desktop and revenue-platform/mobile, and again on A for blog-index/mobile, while it completed with 200 on B in every probe run) -- consistent with a race against teardown timing rather than a stable failure; (3) 200 on direct re-request with the same headers -- a direct fetch() of the exact URLs recorded in this run's visual-suite.json (https://growmax-website.vercel.app/demo?_rsc=JOYFzgqX9X1y8Hxb and .../demo?_rsc=fvVk386B7PbQRK64), sending RSC:1, Next-Router-Prefetch:1 and the bypass header (never argv; read from docs/migration/.scratch/bypass-secret), returned 200, content-type text/x-component, in 446ms and 142ms respectively; (4) A issues the same prefetch for the same path/page/viewport -- the probe's `page.on('request')` capture shows www.growmax.io firing an identical `_rsc=`-tagged, `rsc:1`/`next-router-prefetch:1`-tagged GET /demo for revenue-platform (both viewports) and blog-index (both viewports); on A the /demo prefetch was itself observed aborting (net::ERR_ABORTED) on revenue-platform/desktop and blog-index/mobile in the probe, and completing (200) on the others -- i.e. present and racing on A too, just not necessarily the exact same combination that aborted in the harness's own run (expected, since the abort/complete race is timing-dependent and the probe is a separate run from the harness capture).

Same class as above: the blog index page prefetches every visible post-card link, including this one, and this particular prefetch lost the same navigation/teardown race in this run. RSC markers, cancellation and direct-200 proven exactly as above (the direct re-request of this run's own recorded URL https://growmax-website.vercel.app/blog/b2b-order-management-software-distributors?_rsc=fvVk386B7PbQRK64 with RSC:1/Next-Router-Prefetch:1 headers returned 200, content-type text/x-component, in 356ms). A issues the same prefetch for the same page/viewport: the probe's blog-index/desktop navigation on www.growmax.io shows an identical `_rsc=`-tagged GET to /blog/b2b-order-management-software-distributors, and A's own copy of that exact prefetch aborted with net::ERR_ABORTED in the probe run (A's requestfailed log for blog-index/desktop lists .../blog/b2b-order-management-software-distributors?_rsc=fvVk386B7PbQRK64 -> net::ERR_ABORTED, alongside three other post-card prefetches that also aborted on A in that run: /demo, /blog/ai-helps-distributors-sell-more, /blog/claude-commerce-agents-b2b) -- the same page fires several concurrent post-card prefetches and, on both origins, some race-lose to teardown; which ones is not stable run to run, but the phenomenon (RSC prefetch, aborted, present on A, 200 direct) is identical.

residualFailedRequests.probeMethod: Throwaway script /tmp/rsc-probe.mjs (os.tmpdir(), not committed): launches the same Chromium binary as the reviewed harness with the same proxy-CA SPKI pin, navigates revenue-platform and blog-index at both viewports against both www.growmax.io (no auth header) and growmax-website.vercel.app (bypass header injected via context.route, same mechanism run.mjs uses, read from the bypass-secret file, never passed on argv), captures every `_rsc=`-tagged request's headers/outcome via page.on('request'|'requestfailed'|'requestfinished'), then directly fetch()-es each aborted URL seen on B with its own captured headers plus the bypass header. Full raw output: /tmp/rsc-probe-out/result.json (not committed; contains no secrets -- the bypass header value itself was never printed, only forwarded).

classNote: G5.4's literal criterion (visual pass; no new console errors) and the SPEC-04 §7 extension (new failed requests explained by normalized key) are both satisfied: 20/20 pixel ratios <=0.5%, 0 new console errors, 0 new HTTP error responses, and every one of the 4 flagged newFailedRequestsOnB combinations is a Next.js RSC prefetch abort meeting all four of the task's proof requirements (RSC/prefetch headers, ERR_ABORTED not a real error, 200 on direct re-request, and the identical prefetch present on A for the same page/viewport). This is a slightly larger residual than the prior attempt (2b: 2 combinations, both /demo) because attempt2c is a fresh capture and which concurrent prefetch loses the teardown race is nondeterministic -- the class of residual, and the proof standard it meets, is unchanged.
